scenario.name: Microsoft Threat Intel & Elastic DFIR — ISO / VHD Virtual Disk Mount, Zone.Identifier ADS & LNK Shellbags Forensics
scenario.overview: Think of a bright neighborhood supermarket filled with stocked grocery aisles, rolling shopping carts, barcode price stickers, and busy checkout conveyor belts. Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches. When the store manager reconciles the checkout receipt tape against the aisle inventory count and overhead camera, the swapped barcode trick is caught red-handed. In this scenario (T1566.002, Microsoft Threat Intel & Elastic DFIR, ISO / VHD Virtual Disk Mount, Zone.Identifier ADS & LNK Shellbags Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: container Download, then virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys, then uSRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\\ Navigation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Container Download, then Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys, then USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\\ Navigation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 15 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation (Sysmon EventID 15)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1566.002 - Spearphishing Link & Mark-of-the-Web ADS)
stages.description: Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the checkout cashier go about their routine. When the user downloads Invoice_Oct.vhd from an external webmail link, the browser writes the NTFS Alternate Data Stream Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier containing [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 (Internet), ReferrerUrl, and HostUrl. Sysmon EventID 15 (FileCreateStreamHash) captures the exact Contents of the Zone.Identifier stream (logged in Sysmon Event 15 with EventID=15 , Sysmon FileCreateStreamHash, AlternateDataStream=Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier, ZoneId=3 , URLZONE_INTERNET, HostUrl=https://portal.doc-delivery.net/Invoice_Oct.vhd so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 15 (FileCreateStreamHash): TargetFilename=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 15 , FileCreateStreamHash: TargetFilename=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1566.002 during "Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation , Sysmon EventID 15" , When the user downloads Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ADS Content: [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 ReferrerUrl=https://mail.external-share.com/ HostUrl=https://cdn.external-share.com/Invoice_Oct.vhd runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ADS Content: [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 ReferrerUrl=https://mail.external-share.com/ HostUrl=ht so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1566.002 during "Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation , Sysmon EventID 15" , When the user downloads Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys & Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1 / 12
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1553.005 - Subvert Trust Controls: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass)
stages.description: At the checkout lane, the cashier slides the box across the glowing barcode scanner, which blindly trusts the swapped sticker instead of inspecting what is inside the box. Here in Step 2 inside the supermarket, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the locked stockroom back door. When the user double-clicks Invoice_Oct.vhd, Windows Explorer mounts the virtual hard disk via the VHD Miniport Driver (vhdmp.sys) as drive E:\. Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational logs EventID 1 (VHD surfaced as disk number 2) and EventID 12 (File C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd opened as virtual disk). In this final step inside the supermarket, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches until the receipt tape & aisle camera catches the mismatch.
